items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1959-07-16
items.q: There was an old lady used to give dances back there by the name of Melanson.

ctx.x: Around Dumain. I think it's down around there. I think they call it the cave now. Tony Fusio, I could tell you. Well, anyway, Nappy Lamar goes and books this job, you see. So, we go in there and we, we play all night long. And when we get through, the guy gives us fifteen cents and a pack of cigarettes. See. And, uh, what's that? Wasn't that? So, we went, we told him, uh-uh, we can't wait for that. See. So, he said, well, uh, I'll come back. It'll pick up. Business will pick up. It'll get better, you know. So, he…

back around where the Charlie Hospital is now. It used to be the parish prison, used to be right there in Saratoga and Tulane Avenue. There was an old lady used to give dances back there by the name of Melanson. They never had any electricity in us, just had these lanterns, you know, hanging around. And she'd give us a dollar, maybe a dollar and a half. And the first thing, we had a good band, and the first thing you know, man, the place is getting like that, you see.
